intro: Formal ways to concede a point, however much, and the doubled subjunctive of whatever happens.
p.quieras o no: whether you like it or not
b1.texto:
Formal partners of pero and aunque: **no obstante**, **con todo**, **aun así** begin a new sentence; **pese a** takes a noun or an infinitive; **pese a que**, **si bien** and **aun cuando** take a clause.

However much:

- **por más que** / **por mucho que** + verb
- **por mucho, mucha, muchos, muchas** + noun + **que**
- **por muy** + adjective or adverb + **que**

The mood works as with aunque. A fact takes the indicative: por más que **estudio**, no apruebo. Something open, or brushed aside, takes the subjunctive: por mucho que **insistas**, no iré; por muy caro que **sea**.

The doubled subjunctive means whatever, wherever, however: **digan lo que digan**, **pase lo que pase**, **vayas donde vayas**, **sea como sea**, **quieras o no**.

**Aun** without an accent is even. **Aún** with one is still.
b3.f0: However much I study, I can't manage to pass my driving test.
b3.f1: However hard it is, you'll pass it.
b3.f2: My father says I should give it up. Nevertheless, I'm going to carry on.
b3.f3: Good for you. Whatever they say, you keep going.
b3.f4: Despite the nerves, last time I almost passed.
b5.pregunta: Complete: however much you insist, I won't go.
b5.o0.refuerzo: It is open, or brushed aside: subjunctive.
b5.o1.refuerzo: The indicative would state that you are insisting now.
b5.o2.refuerzo: After que you need a conjugated verb.
b6.pregunta: Complete: however expensive it is, I'll buy it.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Mucho goes with verbs and nouns.
b6.o2.refuerzo: Tan … que is for results, not concessions.
b7.o0.refuerzo: The same verb twice, both in the subjunctive.
b8.pregunta: Which is the most formal partner of «pero»?
b9.o0: Whether you like it or not, you have to go.
b9.o1: If you want, you can go.
b9.o1.explicacion: That would be si quieres, puedes ir.
b9.o2: You don't want to go, do you?
b10.traduccion: However hard I try, I can't.
b11.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write about something you have never managed to do in spite of all your efforts, and something you will do whatever it costs.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Defend aloud an unpopular opinion, conceding points and holding your position.
